Solvent

/SOL-vuhnt/ - the stress falls on SOL · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Solvent means a liquid that dissolves other substances.

A drop of eucalyptus solvent lifted the sticker gum from the new picture frame in seconds.

Worked Example

Dry cleaning is a misleading name for a very wet process. Behind the counter, the machines tumble jackets and gowns through a liquid bath — just never a water bath. The solvent in the drum is chosen for what water cannot do: it carries off body oils, waxes, and greasy films without swelling a single wool fiber, and it evaporates without leaving a ring. The clothes come out having swum, and having never met water at all.

Solvent is the exact word for that liquid, because it names a liquid that dissolves other substances — the active partner in the transaction. Water is the world's commonest solvent, but not the only one, and the cleaner's whole craft is matching the liquid to what must be carried away.

How Solvent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

thinner

thinner: the paint counter's solvent, named for its job of loosening paint

remover

remover: any solvent sold by what it takes off — polish, glue, stain

Antonyms

binder

binder: the ingredient that makes things hold together instead of come apart

sealant

sealant: a coat that locks a surface closed against liquids

How Strong Is It? — cleanser → solvent → acid

cleanser vs. solvent

cleanser vs. solvent: A cleanser lifts dirt off a surface and asks nothing more of chemistry; it is the mild end of this scale.

acid vs. solvent

acid vs. solvent: An acid goes past a solvent — a solvent carries the varnish away and leaves the wood; an acid eats into the wood itself.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of solvent.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — solv-

Root — solv-: to loosen, to release (Latin solvere)

Suffix — -ent

Suffix — -ent: that which does

Put it together

Put it together: Solv- (to loosen) + -ent (that which does) = that which does the loosening. Latin solvere untied knots, freed debtors, and unbound whatever was held fast; a solvent is the liquid that unties a solid, particle by particle. Its unit-mate soluble is the same verb from the other side — the solid that can be untied.

Use the root in a new word: solution

Use the root in a new word: solution: Stir salt into water and the clear result is a solution — the loosened solid spread evenly through the liquid.

Root Check

Word Choice

technical / scientific

Solvent is the workshop and laboratory noun: the liquid that does the dissolving, from water to paint thinner. Its mirror in this unit is soluble, which describes the solid being dissolved — one word for each side of the same event. You will also meet solvent as an adjective meaning able to pay one's debts; that is the same Latin loosening applied to money, and context tells you instantly which one is on the page.
